subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` header make the request-body `model` compatibility metadata, or must `model` continue to be an OpenClaw agent-target id even when the header is present?
rationale: The current code and docs deliberately use an agent-first body `model` contract, while the report gives repeated production evidence that OpenAI SDK-compatible clients send generic model ids and need a header-selected-agent path.

options.title: Let the agent header win
options.body: When `x-openclaw-agent-id` resolves to a valid agent, treat generic body `model` as compatibility metadata and keep backend model changes on `x-openclaw-model`.

options.title: Keep current agent-first contract
options.body: Continue requiring body `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or an OpenClaw agent target even when the header is present, and document the SDK workaround clearly.

options.title: Add explicit compatibility opt-in
options.body: Require a documented opt-in header or mode for generic SDK model values, accepting extra API surface to avoid changing default precedence.

recommendation.title: Let the agent header win
recommendation.body: When `x-openclaw-agent-id` resolves to a valid agent, treat generic body `model` as compatibility metadata and keep backend model changes on `x-openclaw-model`.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent introduced and recently maintained the current agent-first OpenAI-compatible model contract that this decision would change.
